key_insight: Allowing a small finite training error preserves wide, algorithmically accessible solution regions in non-convex neural networks beyond the zero-temperature hard threshold, and these regions can still generalize well.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that injecting or tolerating thermal noise can make hard training regimes more tractable without sacrificing predictive performance, offering a practical route for robust optimization in overconstrained models.
method: Extend the zero-temperature overlap gap property (OGP) to finite temperature with a positive loss tolerance.
Analyze freezing via a criterion based on smoothness of the single-pattern Gibbs weight near the decision boundary.
Use a finite-energy message-passing algorithm to test the predicted accessible regimes numerically.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical derivations plus numerical message-passing experiments showing that thermal noise enables effective generalization in regimes where zero-temperature solutions and teacher recovery are computationally hard.
watch_item: The finite-temperature gains depend on the allowed error level and model assumptions, so the method may not transfer directly to architectures or loss functions that do not satisfy the smoothness/mean-field conditions.
paper_title: On the robustness of noisy solutions in non-convex neural networks
